This side event aims to facilitate dialogue on these emerging issues and identify considerations for future international cooperation.Register to watch online.

daily_top5.title: WHO launches new primary health care course to strengthen health systems globally - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Health is a human right – yet not everyone can access the health services they need, when and where they need them, without financial hardship. Primary health care (PHC) provides a whole-of-society approach to achieving universal health coverage, putting people and communities at the centre of health systems. Despite nearly 50 years of global commitment to PHC, implementation remains fragmented.

daily_top5.title: Is artificial intelligence an aid or an adversary to the global health workforce? - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Join this FREE online webinar held by the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) in collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO).Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping health systems, creating new opportunities and challenges for workforce education, management and planning. This webinar will examine how AI is influencing the skills required of health professionals, transforming workforce deployment and decision-making and shaping national and global health labour markets. Participants will explore key lessons from emerging practice, including both the benefits of AI-enabled innovation and the barriers that may limit its adoption, such as workforce readiness, regulation, ethics and equity concerns.

daily_top5.title: WHO Health Emergencies EPI-WIN webinar: from framework to action: operationalizing emergency ready primary health care for community protection and resilient health systems - World Health Organization (WHO)
daily_top5.summary: Health emergencies—including disease outbreaks, pandemics, climate-related events, humanitarian crises, and natural disasters—are increasing in frequency and complexity. As the first point of contact for most populations, primary health care (PHC) plays a critical role in engaging communities, detecting health threats early, protecting communities and health workers, maintaining essential health services, and supporting rapid emergency response.
